# ContractIQ — Security Plan

**Generated by:** `security-foundation` skill
**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Scope:** Full audit of all `app/api/*` routes, auth flow, and AI input paths against the 8 requirement categories in `skills/security-foundation/SKILL.md`.

This pass is a retrofit, not a greenfield build — the app (built in an earlier session) already had working auth, RLS, and some validation. This document distinguishes what was **already correct** (verified, not assumed) from what was a **real gap** that got fixed.

---

## Issues found and fixed

| # | Area | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | API validation | `upload`, `terms/[id]`, `feedback` routes validated input manually (ad-hoc `if` checks), not via Zod. `process` and `chat` used Zod but returned inconsistent status codes. | Added `termEditSchema`, `feedbackRequestSchema`, `uploadContractTypeSchema` to `lib/utils/validation.ts`. All routes now validate via Zod and return `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` on shape failures, before any business logic runs. |
| 2 | Rate limiting | Only `/api/process` was rate-limited (10/hour, via a Postgres function). `chat`, `upload`, and **login** (brute-force risk) had no limit at all. | New `rate_limit_events` table + `lib/security/rateLimiter.ts` (sliding window, service-role only). Applied to auth (10/min by IP), chat (30/min), process (5/hour — replaces the old DB-function check), upload (20/day). |
| 3 | Prompt injection | No defense beyond the system prompts' own "answer only from X" instructions — a soft suggestion the model usually follows, not a hard boundary. Contract text and chat messages went straight into OpenAI calls unfiltered. | New `lib/security/promptInjectionGuard.ts`. Contract text checked once at upload time (before it's ever stored or sent to any LLM call). Chat messages and custom extraction terms checked on every request. Matches → `400 PROMPT_INJECTION`, request never reaches OpenAI. |
| 4 | Chat/contract ownership | Ownership checks existed inline in each route (`'.eq('user_id', user.id)` + `.single()`), correct but not reusable, and returned `400` instead of `404`. | Extracted into `lib/security/chatSecurity.ts` (`verifyContractOwnership`, `verifySessionOwnership`). Chat route now returns `404` on ownership failure. |
| 5 | File upload | Validated MIME type + size only. A client fully controls its own `Content-Type` header, so MIME-only checking is spoofable. | `lib/security/inputValidator.ts`'s `validateFileUpload()` now checks extension (blocklist + allowlist) → MIME type → size, in that order. |
| 6 | Auth: brute force | `signInWithPassword` was called directly from the browser — a scripted attacker bypasses any client-side throttling entirely by hitting the Supabase API directly. | New `app/api/auth/login/route.ts` — rate limiting (by IP, since there's no user yet) now runs server-side, **before** Supabase is ever called. Login page and `Sidebar` sign-out now call `/api/auth/login` / `/api/auth/logout` instead of the client SDK directly. |
| 7 | Password reset | **No forgot-password flow existed at all** — a user who forgot their password had no way back in. | Added `app/(auth)/forgot-password/page.tsx` and `app/(auth)/reset-password/page.tsx`, linked from the login page. Uses Supabase's standard recovery-link flow (consistent with how signup/email-verification already works in this app — no custom token-exchange route needed). Deliberately shows the same "check your email" message whether or not the address is registered, to avoid account enumeration. |

---

## Verified already correct (no change needed — confirmed, not assumed)

| Area | How it was verified |
|---|---|
| RLS on all 5 original tables | Inserted synthetic rows into every table via the service-role key, then attempted to read them back with the anon key and no session — every single read returned `[]`. Proven, not just declared. |
| Storage privacy | Bucket is private (`public: false`), all access via 1-hour signed URLs, `file_size_limit` and `allowed_mime_types` enforced at the bucket level too (defense-in-depth on top of app-level checks). |
| Env var separation | `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` have no `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix and are only referenced from server-only files (`lib/openai/*`, `lib/supabase/admin.ts`). `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is used exclusively inside `createAdminClient()`. |
| Secret logging | Audited every `console.error` call across `app/api/*` — none log full request/response headers or raw secrets. The one place a raw OpenAI error object is logged, the OpenAI SDK itself pre-redacts the API key in its own error messages. |
| Protected routes | `middleware.ts` already correctly protects `/dashboard`, `/upload`, `/review` and redirects authenticated users away from `/login`/`/signup`. (Not changed to the skill template's generic `/contracts`, `/chat`, `/settings`, `/profile` — those routes don't exist in this app; chat is a tab within `/review`, and there's no settings/profile page.) |
| Cron endpoint auth | `/api/cron/cleanup-storage` already requires a dedicated `CRON_SECRET` bearer token, separate from `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. |

## SQL you need to run

Paste into the **Supabase SQL Editor** (I don't have direct DB execution access — same constraint as every other schema change this session):

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rate_limit_events (
  id         uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id    uuid        REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  identifier text,
  action     text        NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT rate_limit_events_key_present CHECK (user_id IS NOT NULL OR identifier IS NOT NULL)
);

COMMENT ON TABLE rate_limit_events IS 'Sliding-window rate limit log. Service-role access only — see lib/security/rateLimiter.ts.';

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rate_limit_events_user_lookup
  ON rate_limit_events (user_id, action, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rate_limit_events_identifier_lookup
  ON rate_limit_events (identifier, action, created_at DESC);

ALTER TABLE rate_limit_events ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
-- No policies — service role only (default deny for anon/authenticated).
```

(Same content as `supabase/rls-policies.sql` / `supabase/migrations/003_rate_limit_events.sql`.)

**Status: run.** Confirmed live and verified — see "Rate limiting: empirically verified" below.

## Rate limiting: empirically verified

Once `rate_limit_events` was live, each limit was tested against the real running app (not just read from the code) and then cleaned up:

| Endpoint | Configured limit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Auth (`/api/auth/login`, by IP) | 10 / min | 12 rapid attempts → exactly 10 returned `401` (wrong password), 11th and 12th returned `429 RATE_LIMITED` |
| Chat (`/api/chat`, by user) | 30 / min | 32 rapid requests → exactly 30 returned `404` (fake contract, proving they passed the rate check), 31st and 32nd returned `429` |
| Upload (`/api/upload`, by user) | 20 / day | 22 rapid requests → exactly 20 processed, 21st and 22nd returned `429` |
| Process (`/api/process`, by user) | 5 / hour | Seeded 5 rows directly into `rate_limit_events` for a test user (avoiding 5x real OpenAI extraction cost), then made one real request against a real uploaded contract → `429`, confirmed no OpenAI call was made |

All four use the same `checkRateLimit()` function with different configs — the auth/chat/upload tests each landing on the *exact* configured boundary is strong evidence the shared mechanism itself is correct, not just that each endpoint happened to work.

**Bug found and fixed during this pass:** `app/api/upload/route.ts` called `request.formData()` without a try/catch. A request with no body or a non-multipart `Content-Type` (e.g. an empty request, or JSON sent to the wrong endpoint) made `formData()` throw, which was an *uncaught* exception → Next.js's default `500` handler. Confirmed the response body was empty (no stack trace or internal detail reached the client — not a leak), but it was still an ungraceful failure mode standing in the way of the normal validation-error path. Fixed by wrapping the call in try/catch and returning `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` instead.

## Separate pass: browser security headers, secret hygiene (community lab checklist)

A user-provided lab README (`Cohort-Labs/.../03-Security-and-Deployment-Lab/01-security-foundation`) described a *different*, narrower `security-fix` skill covering browser headers and secret hygiene — not present in this repo's `skills/`, but its "Step 3 — Verify the Fixes" checklist was run against the app directly:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Security headers (`X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-XSS-Protection`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`) | **Was failing — fixed.** `next.config.mjs` had no `headers()` export at all. Added all 5 headers plus `poweredByHeader: false`. Verified present via `curl -I` on both pages and API routes after restart (headers require a full server restart, not hot-reload). |
| Unauthorized API call → `401` | Pass |
| No secrets in page source | Pass — scanned `/`, `/login`, `/signup`, `/dashboard`, `/upload` for both the OpenAI key and service-role key value; neither appears |
| `.gitignore` covers env files | Pass — `.env.local` doesn't appear in `git status` |
| Hardcoded secrets in source | Pass — grepped for `sk-...` / `sb_secret_...` patterns across `app/`, `lib/`, `components/`, `hooks/`; none found |
| Unsafe `eval`/`innerHTML` | Pass — no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `eval(`, or `new Function(` anywhere |
| `console.log` of sensitive data | Pass — only `console.error` is used, always with curated objects |

### File modified for this part
```
next.config.mjs — added headers() export (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options,
                   X-XSS-Protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) and
                   poweredByHeader: false
```

## Outstanding / not addressed in this pass

- **`pdf-parse` parser fragility** (flagged earlier this session, unrelated to security): the bundled PDF.js in `pdf-parse@1.1.1` rejects some valid PDFs from certain producers. Not a security issue, but worth fixing separately.
- **Email deliverability**: Supabase's built-in email service is rate-limited; production needs custom SMTP (Resend/Postmark/SendGrid) configured in the Supabase dashboard. Also flagged earlier, not part of this security pass.
- **`is_rate_limited()` Postgres function**: left in place in `database.sql` rather than dropped, since nothing else depends on removing it — but it's no longer called by the app.
